chunks: And from him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who purchased trade goods, and they became stagnant (unsold), while he had already paid the zakat on his wealth before purchasing the goods. When should he pay zakat on them? He said: 'If he kept the goods seeking to recover his principal capital, there is no zakat upon him. And if he held them after he had recovered his principal capital, then upon him is the zakat after he has kept them after the completion of the year of the principal capital.'
He said: And I asked him about a man upon whom wealth is placed (accumulated), and he works with it. He said: 'When the lunar year passes over it, let him pay its zakat.'
ai.seo_question: When should a merchant pay zakat on goods bought with already-taxed wealth?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the nuanced distinction in Shia jurisprudence between goods held for capital preservation versus those held for profit, a key debate in *Fiqh al-Zakat*. It establishes that zakat on trade inventory is triggered by the passage of the lunar year (*hawl*) only after the goods are acquired with the intent of commercial gain, reflecting the Imams' practical approach to commercial transactions. This ruling ensures that merchants are not burdened with double taxation on capital recovery while ensuring timely purification of wealth intended for profit.
